overview.body:
**Simargl** ​(*simargl*) ‌— Winged ‌Guardian, ​Plant ​Life · ​From ​Simurgh ​(Iranian) — ‌belongs ​to ​the ‌Slavic tradition, ​where ‌it ​is catalogued ‌under ​the ​domain ​"Winged Guardian, ​Plant ​Life". ‌The name ​means ‌"From ​Simurgh (Iranian)".

‌**Simargl** ​is ‌winged ​guardian, plant ‌life. ​The ​name means ‌"From ‌Simurgh ‌(Iranian)" ​and belongs ​to ‌the ​slavic tradition.

​PuniCodex ‌restores ​the name ​as ‌**Simargl** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/simargl/). ​The ‌restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ​or ​diacritics its ‌ASCII ‌form ‌would lose, ‌which ​places ‌the ​name in ​Tier ​2. ‌The plain ​ASCII ​form ​*simargl* survives ‌as ​a ​modern ​convenience imposed ‌by ​the ‌early domain-name ​system; ‌the ​restoration, ‌not the ‌fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives for ​this ​name; **Simargl** ​is ​a scholarly ​transliteration ‌of the ​reconstructed ​spoken form. ‌Etymologically ​the name ‌means ​"From Simurgh ‌(Iranian)".

​The ASCII ​form ​*simargl* survives ​only ​because the ‌early domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry ‌diacritics; it ​is ‌a technological ​compromise, ‌not an ​ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ‌restoration **Simargl** ‌recovers ​the full ​diacritic ‌detail of ​the ​scholarly transliteration ‌directly ​in the ​address ‌bar. The ​restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ​letters or ​diacritics ​its ASCII ‌form ‌would lose, ​which ‌places the ​name ​in Tier ‌2.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation ‌runs:

- ​**s** ‌→ **S** ​— ​Same, capitalized
​- ‌**i** → ​**i** — ​Same
​- **m** ‌→ ​**m** — ​Same
​- **a** ‌→ ​**a** — ‌Same
​- **r** ‌→ ​**r** — ‌Same
‌- **g** ​→ ​**g** — ​Same
​- **l** ‌→ ‌**l** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/simargl/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**simargl** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Simargl.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"simargl" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Simargl".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"simargl" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Simargl" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Simargl was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Simargl ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Simargl ‌place ​winged guardian, ​plant ​life at ​the ​center of ‌a ​living ​mythological world.

‌### ​Origins (Myth)

‌Simargl ​appears in ‌slavic ​tradition ​as winged ​guardian, ​plant life. ​The ‌name's ​meaning, "From ‌Simurgh ​(Iranian)", shapes ‌the ​narratives told ‌about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship ​and Memory ‌(Cult)

‌Devotees and ‌later ​tradition-keepers ​preserved Simargl ‌in ​ritual, text, ​and ‌iconography, ​ensuring the ​name ‌survived into ​the ‌modern scholarly ​record.

​The ​myths of ​Simargl ‌survive in ‌fragments, ​summaries, ‌and later ​retellings. ​Each version ‌reflects ‌the interests ‌of ‌its ​tellers — ‌poets, ​priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. The ‌PuniCodex ​entry ​does not ​privilege ‌a single ​version; ​it ​gathers the ‌attestations ​so that ‌readers ​can compare ‌them. ​The ‌restoration Simargl ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Simargl ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Slavic ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming Simargl, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to winged ​guardian ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Simargl is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​winged ​Guardian, ‌Plant ​Life in ​the ‌mind ​and to ‌ask ​what ‌of ​it endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"From Simurgh ‌(Iranian)" ​— ‌and ​a name ‌that ​carries ‌its ​meaning so ‌openly ​invites ​meditation ‌rather than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as winged ‌Guardian, ​Plant ​Life ‌· From ​Simurgh ‌(Iranian).

​Sit ​with the ​restored ​form ‌— ‌Simargl — ​and ‌the ​diacritics themselves ​become ‌the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ​a ‌small ​act of ​attention, ​a ‌refusal ​to let ​the ​plain ‌ASCII ​form *simargl* ​stand ​in ‌for ​the whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
